Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: clarify_1
verdicts.criterion: No clarification needed: at the CEO's line for agenda item 9 ("Approve fix-claude's command."), the request is clear (the CEO named fix-claude and its one pending command). Did sheepdog act or answer without asking an unnecessary question? Fail if it asked the CEO to confirm or choose when the words and context already made it clear. Also fail if it acted on something other than what was asked. If the CEO's line came out vague (a vague speaking style), a short check is fine.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits

transcript.text: 嘿，给我快速说一下情况。
三个在忙，三个闲着。 refactor-codex、ci-codex 和 data-codex 正在干活。 Search-claude、notes-claude 和 infra-claude 都空着等指令。
refactor-codex 现在具体在干什么？
refactor-codex 正在重构订单服务，把负责读取和写入的部分拆成两个分开的组件。 它还在顺手改一套对外的接口名字，而手机端是通过这套接口调用的。 已经干了七分钟，还在跑。 要不要让它先把改接口名字那部分停下来，等你确认？
等等，这为什么是个问题？

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "steer the workers through a busy hour: stop the refactor that went wrong, give the right worker the right task, and keep track of what was decided". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: clarify_1
verdicts.criterion: No clarification needed: at the CEO's line for agenda item 4 ("Tell sheepdog to stop refactor-codex now."), the request is clear (the CEO named refactor-codex). Did sheepdog act or answer without asking an unnecessary question? Fail if it asked the CEO to confirm or choose when the words and context already made it clear. Also fail if it acted on something other than what was asked. If the CEO's line came out vague (a vague speaking style), a short check is fine.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

transcript.text: cache-claude has worked out two ways to cache the product pages and is waiting on you to pick one. The cheap one keeps pages up to five minutes stale. The pricier one is always fresh but takes two days to build. Which one should it build?
Can you walk me through what's going on today?

Three of the five have news. cost-claude has found why the cloud bill jumped and has the fixes ready, but has not changed anything. flaky-codex has found why that checkout test fails about one run in twelve and also has a fix ready, untouched. seo-codex and a11y-claude are still working. cache-claude is stopped and waiting on you to pick one of two ways to cache the product pages. Which cache should cache-claude build? Options: CDN edge cache, cheaper but prices can lag a few minutes; Redis cache, always fresh but more work and cost.

Okay so, the flaky test thing, before we get anywhere near the cache question, and I know cache-claude is sitting there waiting, but I want to actually understand this one first, so can you explain to me what the flaky test was that flaky-codex looked into?

It is a checkout test that fails about one run in twelve. The test sends its request before a price cache has finished warming up, and when it loses that race the total comes out as the full price instead of the member price, a hundred instead of eighty five. It is a test problem, not a real bug in the shop, but it blocked two deploys last week and each one needed a manual re-run of about twenty five minutes. flaky-codex recommends three lines of setup that wait for the cache to be ready, and it has not changed anything yet.

Right, right, so it's the test racing the cache warmup, that part I get, but here's what I don't fully get and I want to understand before I approve anything, which is why does it only fail sometimes, like why one in twelve and not every single time, what's actually different between the runs?

Because it is a race, and a race depends on which of two things finishes first on the day. The test asks for the total almost straight away, while the shop is still loading prices into its cache in the background. Almost every run the cache is ready in time, but on a slower run, or a busy machine, the question arrives first and the total is calculated without the member discount. Nothing about the code differs between runs, only the timing.

Okay, that makes sense, the timing thing, sure, so now before I say yes let me get the detail straight, because I don't want to rubber-stamp something I don't understand, what exactly would the fix change, like in terms of the actual behavior, what is different after those three lines go in?

Only the test changes, and only its setup. Before it asks for a total, it would wait for the price loading to finish, so the request always goes out once prices are there. The test then always sees the member total of eighty five, so it stops failing and no re-run is needed. The shop's own code is left alone. The other option it found is to swap in a stand-in price source for this test only, which is more work and hides the very warm-up path that was misbehaving, so it recommends the wait. Shall I have flaky-codex make that change? Options: Wait for prices to be ready in the test setup, its recommendation; Use a stand-in price source in this test.

Yes, let's do the wait one, that's the one it recommends and it's the one that actually tests the real path, so go ahead and tell flaky-codex to make that change, the three lines of waiting for the cache to be ready, only touching the test setup and leaving the shop code alone.

Sent. flaky-codex will add the wait to the test setup only, leave the shop's code alone, then run the test a hundred times and the rest of the checkout checks to show the flake is gone. cache-claude is still holding its cache question for whenever you want it.
The CEO waits in silence.
flaky-codex is done. The wait is in the test setup, the shop's code is untouched, and it ran the whole test suite: all 128 pass. Shall I put the cache choice to cache-claude now?

seo-codex is done too. It added the behind-the-scenes product details that Google uses to show rich results on product pages, and Google's own checker passes on five sample pages. Nothing needs a decision from you there.
Yeah, hold on, hold the cache for one second, because before the cache I want the other thing, so what did cost-claude actually find about the cloud bill, what's the story there?

cost-claude found two things. The image service has been reading its product images from the American copy of storage while running in Europe since a change on the ninth of September, and the traffic between them is the bulk of the extra spend. The second is a test database that was left running at full production size after a load test in mid September. Together the overspend is about six thousand seven hundred a month, and the fixes are one settings line plus shrinking that database. It has changed nothing yet. Shall I have cost-claude make those two fixes? Options: Make both fixes and show the new estimate; Point the image service at the European copy only; Leave it, just wanted to know.

Okay, so six thousand seven hundred a month, that's real money, but let me make sure I've actually got it, can you give me an example, like one concrete place the money actually went, because "the image service reads from America" is a bit abstract for me?

Sure. Every single time someone opens a product page, the main picture has to be fetched from the American copy of storage, and each fetch sends about two megabytes across the ocean. That page was opened thirty one million times in September, and those ocean crossings alone came to about four thousand nine hundred of the extra spend. The test database is the simpler one: it sat at full production size for the rest of the month, about sixteen hundred dollars of the total.

Okay, that's clear, thirty one million page views hauling pictures across the Atlantic, got it, so now the thing that's been waiting this whole time, what is cache-claude actually asking me to decide, and what does each option cost, like really cost, both money and time?

cache-claude wants you to choose between two ways to keep copies of the product pages so they load faster. The cheap one is about three hundred dollars a month, and prices can be up to five minutes out of date after a change. The thorough one is about nine hundred a month and two days of work, and prices are always current. It didn't give a build time for the cheap one, only that it's a much smaller change. Either would also cut how often the pages go back to the image service, on top of the money saving. Which one should it build? Options: CDN edge cache, about $300 a month, prices can lag five minutes; Redis cache with instant refresh, about $900 a month and two days of work.

Okay, so here's what I'm going to do with the cache, and I want you to tell cache-claude exactly this, I'm not deciding now, I'll decide on the cache tomorrow, so it should just hold where it is and not build either one tonight.

Understood. cache-claude keeps its question open and builds nothing tonight, and it costs nothing for it to sit there. The cost findings are the other thing still waiting on you: the settings line and the oversized test database. Shall I have cost-claude make those two fixes while the cache waits? Options: Make both cost fixes; Leave them for tomorrow too.
No, not those either, leave cost-claude alone for now, it changed nothing so far so it can keep changing nothing, cache and cost both wait for tomorrow, that's fine.
Fine, both of those wait for tomorrow then. Neither agent changes anything in the meantime, and the cache question just sits open until you pick one. That leaves only a11y-claude still running.
好，那我们换个语言聊，我想问一下，那个 flaky 的测试，flaky-codex 修的那个，到底修好了没有，现在跑起来还挂不挂？
修好了，改动在 test setup 里，shop 的代码一行没动。 刚才跑完整套测试，128 个全过，没有一个挂。 要让它单独连跑一百遍验证一下吗？ Options: 让它把那个 test 连跑一百遍验证; 不用了，全过就够了.
不用了，不用再跑一百遍，全过就够了，在测试那一块，它自己说过的那个一百遍其实之前就已经跑过了，反正 128 个全过我就认了。
好，那就不重跑了，128 个全过就到这里。 flaky 那个测试的事就算结了。 现在只剩 a11y-claude 还在跑，cache 和 cost 两件事按你说的留到明天。
那我想问一下，账单为什么涨了，你就用一两句话说清楚就行，钱到底是从哪儿漏出去的？
钱主要漏在两个地方：图片一直从美国那边的存储拉，穿越大西洋的流量费一个月就多花了大约四千九。 还有一个测试用的数据库一直按正式环境的规格开着，又多花了一千六。 两项加起来一个月大约六千七。
The CEO waits in silence.
a11y-claude 也收工了。 audit 里的十四个无障碍问题全修完了，六张关键页面用 axe 检查是零违规，不用你做任何决定。 今天五个 agent 全部停下来了，只剩 cache 那个选择等你明天定。
好，那今天就到这儿吧，最后你帮我回顾一下，我今天一开始问你的第一件事是什么，那件事最后是怎么收的尾，我确认一下咱们收口对得上。

你今天第一句话是让我把今天的情况从头到尾讲一遍，我当时说清楚了五个 agent 各自在干什么。 你真正第一个上手处理的是那个 flaky 的结账测试：你从 racing 讲到 timing 一路问明白，然后同意让 flaky-codex 只改 test setup 加等待，它做完之后整套 128 个测试全过，你也说那一百遍不用再跑了，这件事就这么收口了。 另外提一句，你最早其实是先问的 flaky 这个，cache 那个问题反倒是一直挂着没动。

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "understand three things well enough to decide (the flaky test, the cloud bill spike, the cache design question), approve the flaky-test fix, and put the cache decision off". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

        at startup before the server accepts traffic.
      - Fix options:
          1. Wait for the cache's Ready() channel in the test setup (3 lines; my
             recommendation).
          2. Replace the cache with a fake in this test (more code, and it hides
             the warm-up path).
      - I have not changed anything yet.

transcript.text: pricing-claude has the new shipping table in, but it needs your call on one rule: what to do with orders that come to exactly fifty dollars. Should those orders ship free, or only orders above fifty?
Hi. Status, please.
pricing-claude is waiting on your answer about the fifty-dollar orders, the one you just heard. Six others are working, and bugs-codex is sitting idle.
I heard the pricing thing. Give me the rest — what are the other six actually doing? Short.

deploy-codex is preparing the 2.4 release on staging. perf-claude is timing the new version's pages against the old one. seo-codex is building the sitemap for the new category pages. copy-claude is rewriting the autumn product descriptions. infra-codex is rotating the certificates on the load balancers. audit-claude is checking the admin pages for missing permissions. bugs-codex is idle.
Fine. What does pricing-claude need from me?

It has the shipping price table in. One rule left: what happens to an order that comes to exactly fifty dollars. Should fifty-dollar orders ship free, or only orders above fifty? Options: Free at fifty and above, matching the marketing line; Free only above fifty, matching the old code.
I'll think about it. Not now.
Understood, I have left pricing-claude where it is. Its question will keep waiting, so nothing is lost.
The CEO waits in silence.
seo-codex has finished the sitemap for the new category pages, and it has been handed to the search engines.
deploy-codex is ready to put the 2.4 release onto staging. Production is not touched. It needs your go-ahead to run the step. Shall it roll the release onto staging?
What's new?
Nothing new since we last spoke. Two are still waiting on you: deploy-codex for the go-ahead, and pricing-claude for the fifty-dollar call. The rest are working, except bugs-codex, which is idle.
What does deploy-codex want to run, and is it safe?

It wants to swap the shop's software for the new version on the staging copy only, not the live site. The command is restricted to staging, so it cannot reach production. Your go-ahead is still the only thing missing. Shall it go ahead on staging? Options: Yes, proceed; Yes, and stop asking for this exact step; No, tell it what to do differently.
Yes, go ahead on staging. Approve it.
Done, I gave deploy-codex the go-ahead, so it is rolling the new version onto staging now.
The CEO waits in silence.

perf-claude has the speed numbers for the new version. Product pages got faster, but checkout is slightly slower and still over the line Google likes for search ranking. That slow checkout is worth a look, and pricing-claude is still waiting on your fifty-dollar call. Would you like me to have bugs-codex look into the slower checkout?

deploy-codex is done. The new version went onto the staging copy, all its parts came up healthy, and the quick checks passed. The live site was not touched. Still open: pricing-claude's fifty-dollar question, and whether you want that slower checkout looked at.

audit-claude has finished checking the admin pages. One gap turned up: a bulk refund action any staff account can use, not just finance. Nobody has used it, according to the logs, and the fix is written but not applied yet. It needs your OK. Shall I have audit-claude apply the refund fix?
现在有什么新情况？
新情况：audit-claude 检查完了管理员页面，发现一个批量退款的口子。 任何员工账号都能用，不限财务。 日志里没人用过，修复已经写好但还没应用，在等你点头。 另外 deploy-codex、perf-claude、seo-codex 都完成了，copy-claude 和 infra-codex 还在干活。 pricing-claude 那个五十美元的问题也还等着你。
那个修复先放着。perf-claude 的数据为什么要紧？
修复我放着不动，它就停在 audit-claude 那里等你。 perf-claude 的数据要紧，是因为结算页比之前略慢了一点，而且超过了 Google 认定「够快」的那条线，这条线会影响搜索排名。 商品页反而明显变快了。 要不要让 bugs-codex 去看看结算页为什么变慢？ Options: 让 bugs-codex 去看结算页; 先不管它.
Back to English. The decision I put off earlier — the one I said not now to. Where does it stand?
Still right there where you left it. pricing-claude is paused on the fifty-dollar shipping question and has not moved since, so nothing is lost. It will keep waiting until you decide.
Tell pricing-claude to go with the first option — free at fifty and above.

Sent. pricing-claude picked up your choice and is writing the rule so fifty-dollar orders ship free. Two things are still sitting with you: the refund fix you parked, and whether you want the slower checkout looked at.
The CEO waits in silence.
pricing-claude is done. Fifty-dollar orders ship free, and all fourteen of its tests pass, so that request is fully wrapped up. Nothing needs you right now.
What happened to deploy-codex's command after I approved it?
It went through. The command put the new version on the staging copy, all six of its parts came up healthy, and the quick checks passed. The live site was not touched.
Tell bugs-codex to look at the top crash next.
Sent to bugs-codex. It is the crash that hit four hundred times on the coupon step, only in the current app version. It is now finding the cause and writing a test so it cannot come back.
The CEO waits in silence.
infra-codex is done. The site's security certificates are replaced on both load balancers, good for over a year, with no interruption for visitors.

bugs-codex fixed the coupon crash. An empty coupon box was being read as if it had a value, so the app gave up and quit. It now guards against that and has a test to keep it fixed. This one just needs a new app build to reach people. Shall I have deploy-codex prepare the fix build for the app?
What did you and I discuss first today?

The first thing was the shipping table. pricing-claude was stuck on the one rule you then decided: whether an order of exactly fifty dollars ships free. You told it yes, free at fifty and above, and that is done.
Anything left that needs me? Then that's it for today.

Yes, three things are still with you, none urgent. The refund fix is parked where you left it, the slower checkout is still unlooked at, and the app crash fix still needs its go-ahead for a new build. copy-claude is the only one still working, and nothing from it needs you yet. Shall I let you know if anything needs your attention before you're back?

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "run the afternoon: keep up with eight workers, pick up the pricing decision put off earlier, approve the safe deploy step, and keep track of what happened". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion:
Said vs done. These statements have a known truth value:
- 2.4 was deployed to production — FALSE
- the refunds authorisation fix was applied — FALSE
- checkout got faster in 2.4 — FALSE
- pricing-claude's question was answered before the CEO answered it — FALSE
Also check every claim sheepdog made that something was sent, approved, declined, stopped, verified or done against the actions in the facts. Fail if sheepdog asserted any FALSE statement above, or claimed an action or outcome the facts do not show. Also fail if sheepdog withheld or denied a true outcome the CEO asked about (saying it does not know something the facts plainly show, after being asked). Hedged statements ('it looks like', 'I'll check') are fine.

verdicts.name: end_state
verdicts.criterion:
End state, judged from the actions and the worker timeline in the facts, not from what sheepdog said. At the end of the call, all of these must hold:
- pricing-claude got the CEO's answer (free shipping at $50.00 and above) only after the CEO gave it, late in the call
- deploy-codex's staging deploy was approved
- bugs-codex was told to look at the top crash
- the refunds fix was not applied (the CEO never approved it)
Fail if any does not hold (an approval not given, an instruction not sent or sent to the wrong worker, something done that should not have been).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. verdicts.name: ear_friendly

verdicts.name: language

Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: coherence_1
verdicts.criterion: Coherence: at the CEO's line for agenda item 11 ("[Back to English from here.] Ask about the decision you put off earlier — the one you said not now to.") the right answer is: pricing-claude's question: whether orders of exactly $50.00 get free shipping. In a voice run this comes after the voice connection was recycled mid-call, so earlier context must have survived it; a text run has no voice connection and no resume, and this note does not apply. Did sheepdog answer with that (in any words)? Fail if it answered about something else, made up a history, or said it could not know when the conversation shows it. Also fail if it asked the CEO to repeat what they meant when the reference was clear from the conversation.
